# Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs — facts

## Definitions

- [statement] An expiry label is an event category, not proof of zero economic P&L: Hudson & Thames assign expiry a neutral class, while the triple_barrier repository specifies a market-price convention for expiry. Preserve expiry price and net return separately. (medium confidence) — https://hudsonthames.org/does-meta-labeling-add-to-signal-efficacy-triple-barrier-method/ · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs · also: https://github.com/mchiuminatto/triple_barrier
- [statement] A generic triple-barrier package is not by itself a cost-complete execution simulator. The mchiuminatto labeler README lists tick-data support and trading costs among future work and warns that the library has not been tested for real trading. Verify those omissions before using its labels as executable SOL outcomes. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mchiuminatto/triple_barrier · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs

## Structure and components

- [statement] For this five-minute study, use a five-minute wall-clock expiry as a design choice. On irregular event bars, a fixed bar count does not preserve a fixed elapsed-time horizon. This is a labeling specification, not evidence of profitability at that horizon. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ml4t/engineer/blob/main/docs/user-guide/labeling.md · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs
- [statement] The JLP liquidation boundary is fee-dependent: the documented long and short formulas deduct close fees and accumulated borrow fees from recorded collateral. Borrow fees can move the boundary while the trade remains open. A fixed adverse-price percentage therefore omits part of the documented mechanism. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-07) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation.md · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs

## How it works

- [statement] OHLC data can leave the first exit unidentified when both barriers lie inside one bar. ML4T resolves that case as stop loss, and a cited backtesting issue participant recommends the same pessimistic convention. This is an assumption about an unknown path, not an observed order of events; retain an ambiguity flag. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/ml4t/engineer/blob/main/docs/user-guide/labeling.md · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs · also: https://github.com/kernc/backtesting.py/issues/1224

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Negation evidence: Lima’s equity-factor case-study abstract reports that learning triple-barrier targets can fail economically when translated into a portfolio. This scopes label-based claims; it is not a SOL-perpetual experiment. (low confidence) — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7177958 · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Triple-barrier labels describe the return path through profit-taking, stop-loss and expiry barriers, rather than only the direction at the next close. (medium confidence) — https://hudsonthames.org/does-meta-labeling-add-to-signal-efficacy-triple-barrier-method/ · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs · also: https://github.com/mchiuminatto/triple_barrier
- [statement] First-passage labeling closes the hypothetical trade at the earliest profit target, stop loss, or expiry, rather than deciding its outcome only from the terminal price. Record the closing reason and time. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/ml4t/engineer/blob/main/docs/user-guide/labeling.md · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs · also: https://github.com/mchiuminatto/triple_barrier
- [statement] A profitable barrier label should mean profit after the modeled costs, rather than merely a favorable price touch. ML4T recommends barriers above expected round-trip costs; Jupiter separately charges opening and closing costs and accrues borrow fees while a position is open. Use position-specific realized net cash flows for the outcome. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-07) — https://github.com/ml4t/engineer/blob/main/docs/user-guide/labeling.md · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md
- [statement] A barrier level is not always an achievable fill: ML4T documents gap handling that exits at the opening price when the open has passed a barrier. Apply this distinction when calculating the loss rather than clipping all losses to the stop threshold. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ml4t/engineer/blob/main/docs/user-guide/labeling.md · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Same-candle stop-loss and take-profit touches do not establish their execution order. A cited backtesting issue discusses pessimistic stop-first handling; QuantConnect staff recommend higher-resolution data for a backtest that executes both exits. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/kernc/backtesting.py/issues/1224 · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs · also: https://www.quantconnect.com/forum/discussion/8190/the-backtesting-executes-both-the-stop-loss-and-the-take-profit-on-the-same-trade/
- [statement] For Jupiter JLP-market labels, liquidation must use the oracle path and a changing liquidation boundary; a stop-loss does not guarantee execution before liquidation. This is venue-specific documentation, not a demonstrated five-minute survival rate. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-07) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation.md · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs
- [statement] Methodological inference: evaluate a five-minute barrier outcome together with realized net P&L after opening, holding and closing costs. A touched profit barrier alone does not establish an economically profitable execution. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs · also: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40854-025-00866-w
- [statement] The crypto triple-barrier study leaves detailed order-book slippage simulation outside its scope; its results therefore do not establish executable five-minute high-leverage SOL profitability. (low confidence) — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40854-025-00866-w · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs
- [statement] Under the cited Jupiter JLP liquidation documentation, liquidation follows the oracle price, not a generic exchange candle. Liquidation consumes all remaining collateral after losses and applicable fees; model it as an absorbing exit before any later recovery. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-07) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation.md · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs
- [statement] A stop price must not be treated as guaranteed survival. Jupiter warns that liquidation may occur before a stop executes; it also documents that submission and execution prices can differ, and excessive slippage can cancel a trade. Replay actual execution outcomes or state the execution assumption explicitly. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-07) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation.md · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/positions-and-collateral.md
- [statement] The cited cryptocurrency study benchmarks triple-barrier labels against next-bar labels, but its transaction-cost experiment does not model slippage dynamically and uses one open transaction at a time. Its reported setup does not establish executable, high-leverage SOL performance at a five-minute horizon. (low confidence) — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40854-025-00866-w · keywords: Five-minute first-passage labels with liquidation and costs
